Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Coverage this period is dominated by fallout from the record $6.3 billion Binance crypto hack linked to North Korea, a sharp AI-driven selloff rattling tech and credit markets, and the U.S. midterms colliding with voter anxiety over affordability and inflation. Outlets are also tracking strains in global credit markets, China's economic slowdown, and a wave of corporate restructuring from Wall Street law firms to UK telecoms.

stories.headline: Binance's $6.3 Billion Hack: Inside Crypto's Biggest-Ever Heist
stories.summary: Hackers linked to North Korea stole at least $6.3 billion from Binance in roughly 20 minutes, days after founder Changpeng Zhao had warned that no crypto wallet is fully safe; the exchange says it has since replaced about 95% of stolen assets and resumed withdrawals.

stories.headline: Wall Street Braces for More Volatility After Tech-Led Rout
stories.summary: A fresh bout of market volatility hit stocks after disappointing tech earnings intensified investor anxiety about the sustainability of the AI-driven rally; Bloomberg notes the sell-off was a long-awaited jolt after months of calm.

stories.headline: Credit Markets Hit by 'Bloodbath' as Junk Debt Sells Off
stories.summary: The FT reports that aggressive tactics by borrowers to move assets beyond creditors' reach have intensified a rout in junk debt, rattling credit investors.

stories.headline: China's Economic Activity Loses Steam Sharply in October
stories.summary: WSJ reports a sharp deceleration in Chinese economic activity last month, adding to concerns about the health of the world's second-largest economy.

stories.headline: Trump Struggles to Convince Voters the Economy Is Strong Ahead of Midterms
stories.summary: The Washington Post reports Democrats are framing the midterms as a 'corruption election,' arguing that President Trump and Republicans are enriching themselves while ordinary Americans struggle with inflation and high gas prices; Bloomberg similarly notes Trump is struggling to sell voters on the economy amid affordability concerns.

stories.headline: Europe's Pension Covenant Unravels Amid Fiscal Strain
stories.summary: WSJ examines how European governments are struggling to honor pension promises to future retirees, threatening what it calls a fragile generational contract.

stories.headline: Weil Gotshal to Shut Down After 95 Years in Business
stories.summary: The FT reports the storied Wall Street law firm is closing after an exodus of top talent, raising questions about what happens next for its remaining lawyers and clients.

Business.gaps: Puck and Forbes had no clearly relevant recent business coverage surfaced in search; The Information's most recent AI funding items were older than the 48-hour window.

US politics.overview: With Election Day (Nov. 3) just two days away, political outlets are almost entirely focused on the 2026 midterms: late-breaking shifts in Senate and House ratings toward Democrats, a bitter Michigan Senate endorsement flip, Sen. Chris Murphy's hospitalization, and legal/security flashpoints around the vote including a dismissed DOJ lawsuit in Alaska and new federal subpoenas to election officials. Secondary threads include Trump's legal setback against the Wall Street Journal and data centers emerging as a surprise midterm flashpoint.

stories.headline: Haley Stevens endorses Republican Mike Rogers over Democrat El-Sayed in Michigan Senate race
stories.summary: Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens broke with her party in the race's final days to endorse Republican Mike Rogers over Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed, escalating a feud that began during their bitter primary, with Stevens later appearing alongside Rogers at a Detroit church.

stories.headline: Sen. Chris Murphy hospitalized after stroke
stories.summary: Sen. Chris Murphy (D-Conn.) was hospitalized at Johns Hopkins after suffering a stroke, with his office saying the 53-year-old senator is responding well to treatment.

stories.headline: Judge tosses DOJ lawsuit seeking to block Alaska Senate results if GOP incumbent loses
stories.summary: A federal judge dismissed an unusual Trump administration lawsuit that tried to block certification of Alaska's Senate race results if Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan loses to Democrat Mary Peltola, a ruling that comes as Sullivan himself has publicly committed to accepting the results regardless of outcome.

stories.headline: Final pre-election ratings keep shifting toward Democrats across House, Senate and governor races
stories.summary: In the campaign's closing days, nonpartisan handicappers moved dozens of races toward Democrats — Roll Call counted 63 House race shifts toward Democrats versus one toward Republicans — while Cook Political Report separately moved Kansas and Nebraska's governor's races further left and rates Senate races in Alaska, Iowa, Kansas, Maine, Michigan, Ohio and Texas as toss-ups.

stories.headline: Judge permanently dismisses Trump's $10 billion defamation suit against Wall Street Journal over Epstein letter
stories.summary: An Obama-appointed federal judge dismissed President Trump's defamation lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal over its reporting on an alleged birthday letter to Jeffrey Epstein, marking the second time Trump's claim of actual malice against the outlet has failed.

stories.headline: Federal subpoenas to election officials mark escalating DOJ pressure campaign ahead of vote
stories.summary: Stateline reports that a federal grand jury in California has issued subpoenas to election officials as the Trump administration's Justice Department wages a parallel public and behind-the-scenes legal fight over the ballots of suspected noncitizen voters.

stories.headline: AI data center backlash becomes a surprise force in the midterms
stories.summary: Axios reports that opposition to AI data centers has become a major midterm issue, with voters in 10 states deciding 41 ballot measures and candidates in Texas, Ohio and Utah forced to take concrete positions after Trump complicated matters for the GOP by praising the facilities at a rally.

stories.headline: Political ad spending hits record highs as broadcast TV reaps a midterm bonanza
stories.summary: The New York Times reports that despite marketers' broader shift away from broadcast, local TV stations are cashing in heavily on midterm political ad spending, with Texas races like Paxton-Talarico singled out as especially lucrative.

US politics.gaps: SCOTUSblog and NOTUS had no outlet-specific coverage found in the last 24-48 hours directly on this topic; NOTUS, Punchbowl News, Cook Political Report and Axios items used were the most recent available but some were several days old. Politico, NYT, WSJ and The Guardian coverage was limited to the feed items provided since these outlets block web search.

Tech & AI.overview: Tech and business outlets are dominated by the fallout from a $6.3 billion North Korea-linked hack of Binance and Anthropic's imminent mega-IPO, while a parallel thread runs through nearly every outlet about mounting anxiety over the AI investment bubble, data-center politics, and Wall Street's growing skepticism of hyperscaler debt. OpenAI and Anthropic product/policy changes (ChatGPT monetization shifts, a Cursor extension breach) and legal challenges to AI infrastructure (xAI pollution suit, California's Prop 45) round out the coverage.

stories.headline: Anthropic pushes toward a record-breaking IPO
stories.summary: Anthropic filed publicly for its IPO on October 26 and is expected to list on Nasdaq in November, with formal marketing for the offering set to begin as soon as the week of November 9 in a deal expected to rival SpaceX's record debut.

stories.headline: North Korea linked to $6.3 billion Binance crypto heist as exchange resumes withdrawals
stories.summary: The FBI attributed the massive Binance hack to North Korean hackers it labeled "TraderTraitor," and the exchange has begun phased withdrawals after recovering 95% of the stolen assets.

stories.headline: AI data centers become a flashpoint in US midterm elections
stories.summary: With anti-data-center candidates poised to win in New York, Wired examines what the state's moratorium fight signals for Democrats nationally, while TechCrunch reports that data centers dominated conversation at a Brooklyn midterm event and The Verge flags a California ballot measure that could let developers sidestep environmental scrutiny.

stories.headline: Investors scramble to hedge against an AI bubble as hyperscaler debt costs spike
stories.summary: WSJ reports investors and traders are racing to buy protection against the AI trade as lenders grow choosier and demand stricter terms, while Techmeme notes the cost of insuring against debt defaults at Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle has hit its highest level since 2021.

stories.headline: OpenAI tightens ChatGPT monetization and merges Chat and Work modes
stories.summary: OpenAI is combining ChatGPT's Chat and Work modes into one interface with a shared token-based quota starting in December, a move the outlet says ends unlimited-prompt pricing, following a separate report that OpenAI is now capping paid ChatGPT accounts per device and card.

stories.headline: NAACP lawsuit over xAI data center pollution allowed to proceed
stories.summary: A judge let a lawsuit move forward accusing SpaceX-owned xAI of violating the Clean Air Act with its data center operations.

stories.headline: Anthropic's verified Cursor extension was backdoored for nearly 12 hours
stories.summary: An Anthropic VS Code extension listed on Cursor was compromised for almost half a day, and it remains unclear how attackers gained access to the verified account.

stories.headline: Apple's CEO defends cautious AI strategy
stories.summary: Apple's new CEO pushed back on criticism of the company's AI pace, saying Apple does not want to ship AI features purely for their own sake.

Tech & AI.gaps: No stories from the last 24-48 hours were found for Platformer, VentureBeat, Rest of World, or Google DeepMind; The Information's AI coverage found was older than the window; OpenAI itself had no fresh (within 48h) company blog post beyond older DevDay and policy items.

Energy.overview: Energy and climate coverage right now is dominated by the fallout from the Iran conflict's effects on Gulf shipping and the broader oil-and-gas trade, alongside a UN biodiversity summit outcome and routine U.S. utility investment news. Specialist clean-energy trade press (Heatmap, Canary Media, Latitude Media, Utility Dive) had no stories published within the last 24-48 hours in available search results, with their most recent substantive coverage running from roughly a week to over a month old.

stories.headline: Pakistan LNG Cargo Attacked Near Hormuz Had Iranian Approval
stories.summary: Bloomberg reports Pakistan had negotiated safe-passage terms with Iran for the LNG carrier Al Mayeda before it was attacked near the Strait of Hormuz, underscoring how fragile shipping security has become in the chokepoint even with prior diplomatic arrangements.

stories.headline: How a Little-Known Company Dominated the Persian Gulf Oil Trade
stories.summary: The New York Times profiles South Korea's Sinokor, which now controls roughly half of all tanker transits through the Strait of Hormuz after a timely bet made just before the Iran war began.

stories.headline: Russia's Shadow Fleet Turns to Nets and Rubber Tires for Makeshift Drone Armor
stories.summary: The Wall Street Journal details how Russia's sanctioned oil-export tanker fleet is improvising crude drone defenses as Ukraine intensifies strikes on vessels that help finance Moscow's war effort.

stories.headline: COP17: Key Outcomes Agreed at the UN Biodiversity Conference in Yerevan
stories.summary: Carbon Brief reports that negotiators at the COP17 biodiversity summit in Yerevan completed the first global stocktake of progress toward the 2030 nature-loss-reversal targets, a milestone for tracking whether countries are on pace to meet their pledges.

stories.headline: Xcel Energy Rolls Out $70B, 5-Year Capital Plan Focused on Renewables
stories.summary: Utility Dive reports Xcel Energy unveiled a five-year, $70 billion capital plan built around 9.2 GW of renewables and 2.3 GW of storage, with CEO Bob Frenzel framing it as a way to meet surging demand while still cutting emissions.

Energy.gaps: No stories from the last 24-48 hours could be confirmed for Heatmap, Canary Media, or Latitude Media — their most recent available coverage was roughly a week to several months old. E&E News and Argus Media were not reachable within the four-search limit for this round and no feed items were supplied for them, so no current coverage is reported for those two outlets. Reuters, FT, and The Economist also had no feed items provided and could not be checked via search.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage is dominated by the fallout from the Communist Party's fifth plenum, which concluded last week with a landmark party-building document extending political control into the tech sector, alongside a reshuffled military leadership. Economic data showing a surprise contraction in factory activity, record EV sales divergence among automakers, and ongoing debate over China's export-driven growth model round out the business coverage, while several outlets examine growing social anxiety among Chinese youth.

stories.headline: Fifth plenum document extends party control into tech, crypto and gig economy
stories.summary: A newly released plenum document formally codifies "Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building" and orders expanded party cells and digital anti-corruption tools across internet platforms, crypto and gig-economy firms, with companies required to embed party building into their corporate charters.

stories.headline: China's factory activity unexpectedly contracts in October
stories.summary: State-run Xinhua reports the official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 in October from 50.1 in September, with officials attributing the slide to front-loaded demand before the National Day holiday and a complex global environment, even as high-tech manufacturing kept expanding.

stories.headline: Military anti-corruption chief Zhang Shengmin promoted to Politburo
stories.summary: Zhang Shengmin, described as Xi's "lone hatchet man" in the military, has become the last general remaining at the top of China's armed forces after an unexpected promotion to the Politburo following a wave of purges.

stories.headline: Chinese EV makers post sharply diverging October sales
stories.summary: BYD, Geely and Chery posted record or near-record October sales with BYD's battery-electric vehicles topping 300,000 for the first time, while Nio, GWM and Huawei-backed HIMA all reported year-on-year declines, with HIMA deliveries halving.

stories.headline: Caixin commentary defends China's record trade surplus amid criticism
stories.summary: A Caixin commentary argues that China's merchandise trade surplus, which reached nearly $940 billion in the first nine months of 2026, up 7.8% from a year earlier, does not by itself prove an economy out of balance despite mounting criticism from the US, EU and IMF.

stories.headline: China's AI labs race toward recursive self-improvement without touching model weights
stories.summary: Pandaily reports that Zhipu, DeepSeek, ModelBest, Moonshot AI, Alibaba, ByteDance and Xiaomi are all pursuing recursive self-improvement techniques, focusing on the machinery and tooling around AI models rather than the model weights themselves.

stories.headline: Hit podcasts expose anxieties of China's youth, worrying officials
stories.summary: The Economist reports that a boom in Chinese podcasts airing young people's frustrations over jobs and daily life is drawing increasing government scrutiny.

stories.headline: Chinese state TV skips La Liga broadcast after Mbappe's Mao joke
stories.summary: Chinese state television did not broadcast the first La Liga matches since Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe sparked anger with a joke about former leader Mao Zedong.

China.gaps: No recent China-beat coverage was found via search for The Wire China, Sixth Tone, China Media Project, Rest of World, Yicai Global, TechNode, or Focus Taiwan; Reuters, AP, FT, NYT and additional WSJ items beyond the provided feed could not be checked since these outlets block search.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Coverage across Gulf and Middle East outlets is dominated by the fallout from the Qatar LNG tanker attack and the parallel US-Iran diplomatic push in Doha ahead of the November 3 US midterms, alongside Israel's ongoing Hebron siege and Gaza strikes. Business-focused outlets (AGBI, Zawya, Arabian Business) are tracking the economic toll of the eight-month war, from GCC growth downgrades to rising living costs.

stories.headline: Qatar LNG tanker Al Mayeda struck in Gulf, sparking regional condemnation
stories.summary: Qatar's LNG carrier Al Mayeda was hit by unidentified objects while sailing in the Gulf on Friday evening, with Doha calling it a dangerous act threatening maritime navigation and global energy supplies and warning it reserves the right to take necessary measures. Saudi Arabia separately condemned the attack and called for urgent international action to protect shipping and global energy supplies.

stories.headline: Iranian negotiators hold third day of Doha talks to avert renewed war
stories.summary: Iranian negotiators were in Doha for a third straight day of talks with Qatari mediators aimed at ending the US-Israeli war, with the discussions coordinated in regular contact with Washington amid fears the conflict could reignite after the November 3 US midterms. Iran's Supreme Leader ordered the armed forces to be prepared for renewed strikes even as both sides signaled some diplomatic movement.

stories.headline: Hebron siege enters 10th day as Israel threatens wider West Bank offensive
stories.summary: Israeli forces maintained their lockdown of Hebron for a 10th day, with the city's mayor estimating daily economic losses exceeding $3.8 million and more than 3,300 Palestinians displaced or affected as homes were demolished and over 300 businesses closed. Israeli troops also arrested Palestinian teachers near Hebron and raided a UN-run school in East Jerusalem's Shufat camp on Sunday.

stories.headline: Israeli strikes kill at least eight in Gaza as ceasefire violence continues
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed at least eight Palestinians, including five police officers, in two separate attacks on Gaza on Sunday, according to medics, part of continued violence despite the nominal ceasefire. Middle East Eye separately reported strikes killing nine people including a child the same day.

stories.headline: IMF projects GCC economy will contract 4.8% in 2026 on war disruption
stories.summary: The IMF's October Regional Economic Outlook sharply downgraded 2026 growth for the six GCC economies, projecting a 4.8% contraction this year followed by a 9.1% rebound in 2027 as the Middle East conflict disrupts hydrocarbon production, shipping and trade. Kuwait is seen facing the steepest contraction at 16.7%, followed by Qatar at 15.6% and Bahrain at 11.3%, while Oman is the only member expected to grow.

stories.headline: Gulf living costs climb even as headline inflation stays contained
stories.summary: AGBI reports that GCC inflation remains subdued overall despite the Iran war's impact on global energy and commodity prices, but food and transport costs are rising sharply, with Dubai's annual inflation hitting a four-year peak of 5.7% in June before easing to 5.03% in September. Analysts warn further consumer price increases are likely as regional conflict continues to heighten cost pressures.

stories.headline: Houthis renew threats against Saudi Aramco and aviation
stories.summary: Houthi media, citing an anonymous military official, repeated threats on Sunday against Saudi oil giant Aramco and aviation inside the kingdom, adding to regional tensions over maritime and energy security.

stories.headline: South Korea's Sinokor emerges as dominant player in Hormuz oil trade
stories.summary: A little-known South Korean shipping company, Sinokor, has come to control roughly half of all tanker transits through the Strait of Hormuz, having placed a large bet just before the Iran war began.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: Could not find current, distinct coverage from Khaleej Times, Saudi Gazette, Al Arabiya English, Ynetnews or Haaretz beyond outdated cached pages; Reuters, AP, FT and BBC block search and had no relevant feed items provided.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Coverage across these outlets this week centers on the worsening Ebola outbreak in Congo, warnings about democratic backsliding from the Mo Ibrahim Foundation, and a cluster of African fintech and payments news out of TechCabal's Moonshot conference in Lagos. Business-focused outlets are also tracking a large Madagascar mining and energy financing deal, South African banking leadership, and organised-crime pressures on investment in South Africa.

stories.headline: Ebola deaths in Congo surpass 5,000 as fears of regional spread grow
stories.summary: Deaths in the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak have passed 5,000 as the government struggles to contain the disease, with cases now appearing in other African countries.

stories.headline: Mo Ibrahim Foundation warns Africa is suffering through a 'strongmen' era
stories.summary: The governance watchdog's latest index finds broad gains in economic opportunity and human development over the past decade but steep declines in security, human rights and public participation across the continent.

stories.headline: Madagascar seeks $5bn with Gemcorp for energy and mining push
stories.summary: Madagascar is partnering with asset manager Gemcorp Capital Management in a bid to raise as much as $5 billion to fund energy, infrastructure and mining projects on the island, according to a Bloomberg report carried by Mining Weekly.

stories.headline: Putin's latest African outreach meets scepticism
stories.summary: African Business reports that Russian President Vladimir Putin's newest charm offensive toward African governments is being greeted with growing wariness across the continent.

stories.headline: African fintechs push tap-to-pay, AI payments and dollar-free cross-border rails
stories.summary: At TechCabal's Moonshot conference in Lagos, executives from Verve, Grey and OPay described plans for phone-based tap-to-pay, AI-driven payments and intra-African payment rails meant to cut cross-border friction and reduce dollar dependence, while other panellists flagged that stablecoins still face cost and security hurdles.

stories.headline: Inside Kenny Fihla's rise to the top of South African banking
stories.summary: The Africa Report traces how three decades of trade-union activism, municipal turnarounds and financial-sector experience built Kenny Fihla's pan-African network, which he is now using atop South African banking group Absa.

stories.headline: Cape Verde presidential campaign kicks off with Neves rally
stories.summary: Campaigning has formally begun in Cape Verde's presidential election, with incumbent José Maria Neves drawing hundreds of supporters to a rally in São Vicente.

Africa.gaps: Africa Confidential's and The Continent's most recent available content predates the 48-hour window (Africa Confidential's latest dispatches are from mid-to-late October, and The Continent's latest located issue is from early September), so nothing from them could be confirmed as current. Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT and WSJ block direct search and had no Africa-specific items in the provided feed, so their current coverage could not be assessed.

Media.overview: Media-trade coverage over the last two days centers on the deepening economic fight between news publishers and AI companies (court filings on traffic collapse, Meta's scraping-terms fight in Scandinavia), plus ongoing turmoil in TV news access and staffing. Entertainment trades (Variety, THR, Deadline, TheWrap) were dominated by box office and Halloween/SNL content rather than media-industry business news this cycle.

stories.headline: Publisher coalition tells court AI retrieval is 'already eating away' at traffic and revenue
stories.summary: A Digital Content Next court filing backing the NYT and other publishers' copyright suit against OpenAI and Microsoft found unique visitors to member sites fell sharply, citing a Carnegie Mellon/Indian School of Business study that Google AI Overviews cut outbound clicks to publishers by nearly 40%.

stories.headline: Global publishers unite against Meta's new AI scraping terms after Norwegian court win
stories.summary: An Oslo court ruled Meta's new ad/business terms must face legal review before taking effect, as publisher bodies in Norway, Denmark, Sweden, Canada and the UK's competition regulator all moved against Meta, with one Canadian publishing CEO saying Meta's move has done "more to unite publishers around the world than anything" he's seen.

stories.headline: Broadcast TV cashes in on midterm political ad surge even as marketers shift elsewhere
stories.summary: Local broadcast stations are seeing a political-ad bonanza during the midterms, with Texas singled out as a prime example even as overall marketer spending drifts to other media.

stories.headline: Bloomberg reportedly paying Truth Social $100,000 a month for faster access to Trump's posts
stories.summary: Nieman Lab flagged a Reuters report that Bloomberg is paying for a Truth API service to get quicker access to President Trump's posts, in what Reuters said "likely mark the first time a business tied to a sitting president has sold access" this way.

stories.headline: Paula Reid joins MS NOW as Chief White House Reporter amid ongoing access fight
stories.summary: Adweek reports Paula Reid's hire comes as CNN, MS NOW and Politico continue amending their lawsuit over White House press-pool access.

stories.headline: Agencies face a staffing rethink as workplace AI tension grows
stories.summary: Digiday reports that AI agents are becoming common inside agencies, and while most firms haven't yet grasped how to reshape teams around them, the moment presents a window to rethink staffing.

stories.headline: Telegraph to cut around 100 jobs as it pushes to become a 'global, AI-powered' outlet
stories.summary: Press Gazette's news tracker reports the Telegraph is cutting roughly 100 roles as part of a push to be a 'global, AI-powered' business, coming just months after its Axel Springer takeover.

stories.headline: How the WSJ pierced a US military blackout on Iran base damage
stories.summary: The Journal detailed its own investigative methodology, describing how reporters combined tens of thousands of satellite images, Iranian media statements and a custom computer program to assess damage to US bases.

Media.gaps: No verifiable fresh (24-48h) coverage was found from Status, Puck, Columbia Journalism Review, Poynter, Bloomberg, FT, or The Guardian; Variety, The Hollywood Reporter, Deadline, TheWrap and Mediaite feed items in this window were dominated by entertainment/box-office/celebrity content rather than media-industry business news.
